title: Granting Foster Parents Access to Relevant Health Information of Children Under Their Care
what_it_is: Granting Foster Parents Access to Relevant Health Information of Children Under Their Care

sections.label: Foster parents' access to information
sections.summary: MSF shares information with foster parents when necessary, and foster parents get an MSF letter identifying them as caregivers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: When necessary, MSF will share this information with foster parents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: If parents refuse to provide the information, MSF’s Child Protective Service can exercise powers under the Children and Young Persons Act to obtain and share medical information of the child, if needed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Since fostering is a temporary arrangement, foster parents do not have direct access to the foster child’s health records via HealthHub or Health Buddy applications, as access remains tied to the birth parents’ Singpass.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: However, foster parents are issued a letter from MSF that identifies them as caregivers under the Ministry’s fostering scheme.

sections.label: Foster child medical fee exemption
sections.summary: Every foster child gets a medical fee exemption card, and a foster care worker supports each placement with face-to-face contact every two months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Every foster child is issued a medical fee exemption card (MFEC) and this covers standard medical or dental treatment charges as well as compulsory immunisations and medications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: What happens in every foster placement is that there will be a foster care worker that is assigned to support both the foster parents as well as the foster child, and they will have at least one face-to-face contact every two months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Every foster parent can raise any concerns or difficulties that they face during these sessions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Every once in a while, I will also get feedback from foster parents as to how we can improve the process to help facilitate their work in taking care of the foster child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: We will continue this engagement and make sure that, wherever support is required, we will render them as soon as possible.
